hints: Identify the fixed members: Ranuf must travel in the coach and Saed must travel in the car, so both assignments are predetermined.
Determine the remaining choices: subtract the 2 fixed individuals from the total 40 members to find how many unassigned people remain.
Calculate the remaining seats to fill in the coach: since Ranuf already takes 1 of the 35 coach seats, 34 coach seats remain.
Set up the combination \binom{38}{34} or equivalently \binom{38}{4} (choosing the remaining 4 car passengers) and evaluate.
walkthrough:
Identify the number of remaining members and remaining coach seats:
$$\text{Remaining members} = 40 - 2 = 38$$
$$\text{Remaining coach seats} = 35 - 1 = 34$$

Express the number of ways to choose the remaining coach passengers using combinations:
$$\text{Number of ways} = \binom{38}{34} = \binom{38}{4}$$

ai_rubric.Handling Selection Restrictions: Accounts for the predetermined assignments of Ranuf and Saed by reducing both the pool to 38 and the required coach seats to 34 (or car seats to 4).
ai_rubric.Calculating Combinations: Sets up and calculates 38C34 or 38C4 correctly to obtain 73815.

teacher_walkthrough: We have a club of 40 members traveling in two vehicles: 35 in a coach and the remaining 5 in a car.

Two specific members have fixed travel assignments:
Ranuf is already assigned to the coach.
Saed is already assigned to the car.

Because these two people have fixed assignments, neither of them is available to be chosen freely among the remaining seats:
$$\text{Available members} = 40 - 2 = 38$$

Ranuf fills 1 seat in the coach, so the coach now needs:
$$35 - 1 = 34 \text{ additional passengers}$$

Since the order in which passengers enter the coach does not matter, we use the combinations formula:
$$\binom{n}{r} = \frac{n!}{r!(n - r)!}$$

By symmetry of combinations, $\binom{n}{r} = \binom{n}{n - r}$, so $\binom{38}{34} = \binom{38}{4}$. Expand the numerator and denominator:
$$\binom{38}{4} = \frac{38 \times 37 \times 36 \times 35}{4 \times 3 \times 2 \times 1}$$

Simplify the product step by step:
Numerator:
$$38 \times 37 = 1406$$
$$1406 \times 36 = 50\,616$$
$$50\,616 \times 35 = 1\,771\,560$$
Denominator:
$$4 \times 3 \times 2 \times 1 = 24$$

Divide the numerator by the denominator:
$$\frac{1\,771\,560}{24} = 73\,815$$
Alternatively, selecting the 34 coach passengers automatically leaves the remaining 4 members to fill the remaining 4 seats in the car.
